case: NACA0012, alpha=4.0 deg, Re=6e6, incompressible kOmegaSST, fully turbulent
purpose: Grid + convergence-depth sensitivity for the production medium mesh

runs.note: stopped at iteration cap mid-relaxation; excluded from grid comparison
CL still drifting slowly (~+0.003/1000 iters) at cap; std criterion met

findings: At equal convergence depth (6000 iters): CL spread across coarse/medium/fine is 0.4311-0.4336 (0.6%); medium-vs-fine CD differs by 0.7% - the production medium mesh is inside the asymptotic range at this operating point.

Convergence depth is the dominant uncertainty, not mesh refinement: at 3000 iters both medium and fine sit on a slowly-relaxing transient (CL inflated ~1.3% medium / ~6.8% fine, CD deflated ~2.4% medium).

The campaign std-window criterion (CL std < 5e-4 over 100 iters) is met at 3000 iters on medium but catches only part of the drift; systematic bias bounded ~1.3% CL, ~2.4% CD for the production dataset.
Coarse-mesh CD (+10% vs medium/fine) shows the under-resolved near-wall region over-predicts drag; medium and fine agree.
Fine mesh needs >= 6000 iterations for steady statistics; the campaign uses only medium, so no campaign impact.
campaign_implication: Medium-mesh / 3000-iter production settings introduce <= ~1.5% CL and <= ~3% CD systematic uncertainty from convergence depth at alpha=4; acceptable for surrogate training and flagged for the report's V&V section.
